I don’t hear voices or anything, but there’s this quiet certainty that things aren’t as they seem. I can’t explain it. My boss asked if I was okay last week. I look tired. I *am* tired. I know I look different—my clothes hang off me—but in the mirror, I still see myself as heavy, like I’m hiding fat under my skin. It doesn’t make sense, I know, but the thought of gaining weight feels like a nightmare coming true. I feel like food is the enemy, and if I give in, it’ll ruin everything. I haven’t been hearing voices or anything like that—this isn’t about being “crazy” in that way. It’s just this constant fear: eating equals becoming someone I can’t stand.

I’ve always been particular about routine—working among the quiet order of books suits me. Lately, though, even that feels overwhelming. I just don’t feel right eating like I used to. I eat a bite or two—sometimes half a banana, a few crackers. Not because I’m not hungry, but because… I can’t. The idea of food sitting in my stomach, changing my body—it terrifies me. Like I’ll balloon, no matter what I eat. I’ve lost weight, yes, my clothes hang off me now, but I still see someone who could slip into heaviness too fast.  

People at work keep asking if I’m sick, if I’m sleeping. They don’t understand. I’ve tried explaining, but they don’t listen. The truth is, I feel like someone’s watching, like the books know when I eat. Sometimes I think the shelves shift when I’m not looking—like they’re judging. I don’t know if that’s real or not, but it feels real. I don’t talk about it because no one would believe me—except maybe that the food is being poisoned? Not poison exactly, but… changed. Altered to make me gain. I don’t want to risk it.  

It’s been months now. I don’t know what’s wrong, only that I can’t eat, can’t trust my body, can’t shake the feeling that everything’s watching.

I eat just a few bites a day—sometimes half a banana or a spoonful of yogurt—not because I’m not hungry, but because eating more feels dangerous. I weigh myself every morning, and even when I see how thin I’ve gotten, I can't bring myself to eat. I’m down to 98 pounds now, and still losing.  

I know I’m thin, but I *feel* like I’m carrying weight I don’t have—like my body is betraying me, expanding when it’s actually shrinking. I’m terrified that if I eat, I’ll balloon up, lose control. People say I look unwell, but that just makes me more convinced I’m doing the right thing—staying in control.  

Sometimes I think others are trying to sabotage me—like when my coworker offered me a muffin, I wondered if she wanted me to fail. But it’s not that I hear voices or think the government is watching. It’s just… food and my body feel like enemies. The fear isn’t irrational to me—it’s survival.

I run the warehouse floor every day, so staying lean helps me keep up. I’m down to 138 pounds now, and my wife says I look too thin, but I feel fine—strong, even. The doctor brought it up, said I should gain a few pounds, but that’s just standard advice. They always worry about weight, same way they push vaccines.

I know what goes into my body better than anyone. I don’t eat what I don’t trust. Some things—like how certain oils are contaminated or how refined carbs are secretly laced with chemicals—it’s not paranoia if it’s true. I can’t take chances. My wife thinks I’m overdoing it, says I’ve changed. But she doesn’t see what I see.

I don’t feel hungry most days, and honestly, food feels… risky. Not like I’m afraid of getting fat—that’s not it at all. It’s about control, about staying alert. I’ve been this way for months now, and I’m managing work just fine. If anything, I’m sharper.

My job at the warehouse is actually easier now; climbing ladders, rushing between aisles—I’ve got energy.  

The doctor says I’m underweight, but I told him he’s misreading the numbers. I *know* what my body looks like. I weigh myself every morning, take progress photos. I see how things could go wrong if I let up, even a little.  

Sometimes I think people are watching me eat—like it’s a test. Not that they’re plotting or anything strange… it’s just that I know if I slip, they’ll judge me for getting soft. But it’s my body. I *have* to control it. If I eat like other people, I’ll balloon up. I look in the mirror and see fat everywhere—especially around my gut—no matter what the scale says.  

My wife says I’m scaring her. But she doesn’t understand: thin is safe. Thin is control. Eating “normally” would ruin everything.

D021-D005_h022.question_both:
I’ve always been disciplined—especially with work. As a pilot, you have to be. Lately, though, I just don’t feel right. My appetite’s gone—some days I eat two bites and feel like I’m full. My wife keeps saying I’m fading, that I’ve lost too much weight, but I tell her I’m fine. Planes require precision, and I’m just applying that to my life. I *can’t* gain weight. Not now. Not ever. It feels like… if I do, something bad happens. I can’t really explain it—just a knowing, you know? Like it’s wired into me.

She wanted me to see a doctor, so I went. They were concerned, asked if I was afraid of getting fat. That’s not it exactly. I’m not fat. I’m not thin. I just *need* to stay like this. They said I’m obsessed, but they don’t get the signals I get—the way my body feels when I eat. Like it’s rejecting it on a deeper level, like I’d be corrupting something essential.

Sometimes, I notice things others don’t—patterns in sounds, like radio static speaking in codes. It’s subtle. Not everyone hears it, but it’s real to me. I don’t talk about it much. No one would understand. Why would they?
D021-D005_h022.question_a:
I’ve always prided myself on discipline—flying commercial jets for over 20 years, managing long-haul flights across time zones, staying sharp for my crew and passengers. But lately, the thought of eating more than a bite or two feels… dangerous. I’ll have a single spoonful of rice, maybe some plain chicken, and that’s it for the meal. My wife keeps saying I’m disappearing, that I’m “too thin,” but I know what I see in the mirror—that’s not fat, that’s control.  

I can’t risk gaining weight. Not because of my job—I'm still strong, still capable—but because if I let go even a little, I feel like I’ll spiral. Doctors have measured me, said I’m underweight, but I tell them they don’t understand. They keep pushing nutrition, as if I’m irrational. But I’m not—I know exactly what I’m doing.  

Sometimes, I hear voices during layovers—whispers in hotel rooms, saying things like “you’re still not clean.” But those aren’t about food. The food rules? Those make sense to me. I see my body clearly, even if others say I don’t. Losing weight is the only thing keeping me safe.

If anything, the weight loss is a side effect, not the goal. I hear voices sometimes, especially at night, telling me what’s pure and what’s poisoned. I know this sounds strange, but I can’t ignore the truth I’m being shown. I’m staying alert, staying pure—because what if I’m the only one who sees it?

I check my weight twice a day, every day, and if it goes up even half a pound, I skip dinner and do extra laps around the unit during my break. At first, my coworkers joked about nurses being the worst patients, but they don’t see what I see.  

I know I’m thin—I can feel my ribs, and my clothes hang off me—but I can’t afford to let go. Not with everything I know. Food… it’s not just fuel. It feels like a test. Like if I lose control, other things will unravel. I’ve even started noticing that some of the meal trays look off—like the portions are meant for *me*, not the patients, and the kitchen staff are using it to send messages.  

The doctor says I’m underweight, that I need to gain, but I’m functional. I still work full shifts, take care of my patients, manage my home. I’m not sick like that. I just need to stay sharp. And if I eat more, I’m afraid… I don’t know what happens, but I *know* it’s dangerous. It’s not vanity. It’s protection.

I usually skip breakfast because I’m asleep, lunch gets left in a bag, and dinner—well, I eat a little, but not much. I try to stick to plain things: rice, steamed vegetables. If I eat anything heavy, like meat or pasta, I feel like I’ll gain weight overnight. My clothes still hang loose, but I don’t worry. People at work say I look thin, but I feel fine.

I get dizzy sometimes, especially when I clock out and go from the bright lights to the dark parking lot. My hair’s been falling out more lately—clumps in the brush—but I don’t link it to anything. My period stopped a while back, but I figured it was stress or age. I’ve been like this, more or less, for the past seven or eight months.  

There are also things—thoughts—that keep coming back. I know it sounds strange, but I feel like the food on the line… it’s not just food. Like, when I pack it, I’m part of a system altering people’s minds. Not intentionally, but it’s coded, somehow. I don’t talk about it much. But it affects what I’ll eat. I mean, I know others don’t see it, but it feels real. I just can’t explain it right.

I don’t eat much—skipped breakfast again today, and I usually just push my dinner around when I get home in the morning. High-calorie foods scare me. Like, if I eat a burger or even pasta, I feel certain I’ll gain weight immediately, no matter how little I eat. I know people say it doesn’t work that way, but I can *feel* it happening. My body just feels… wrong when I think about food.

I’ve been dizzy a lot, and I lost so much hair that I had to cut it short. My period’s been gone for over a year, but I figured it’s just stress or the shift work. Doesn’t seem that important, honestly. I look in the mirror and still see someone who needs to lose more. Everyone keeps asking if I’m depressed or "losing my mind," but I’m not hearing voices or anything. I’m not paranoid. I just *know* that if I gain weight, everything will fall apart. I control the food, I control my body—I have to.
D021-D005_h024.question_b:

I haven’t had my period in over a year, and I’m always dizzy on the line, but what does that matter if I’m trying to stay alert? My hair’s thinning, but I can’t focus on that—I’ve got to watch for the patterns. People think I’m just not eating to stay thin, but I’m not afraid of gaining weight. I’m afraid of ingesting the signals. The government puts tracking enzymes in cooked food, and if I eat, they’ll know where I am. That’s why I only eat raw vegetables now—when I can trust them.
